{category}geography.short_description: Geographic FIPS code as a string: 5-digit county code in demographics_county.parquet; 2-digit state code or '00' (national) in demographics_state.parquet. Includes Puerto Rico (72) and its municipios.

{category}time.short_description: Year-end date (YYYY-12-31) of the data vintage. ACS 5-year measures cover 2019-2024, where each year is the end year of a 5-year estimation window; PEP measures are a single 2023 vintage.

{category}source.short_description: Census program the row's value came from. ACS 5-Year and PEP measure overlapping concepts with different methodologies and are reported side by side rather than reconciled.

{category}measure.short_description: Identifier of the measure in this row; the name matches the source column in the census standard file.

{category}value.long_name: Value of the demographic measure identified by measure
{category}value.short_description: Value for the measure identified by the `measure` column. Units differ by measure: `acs_POP*` and `pep_population` are person counts, `acs_PCT_*` and `pep_pct_*` are proportions (0-1), `acs_AGE` is years, `acs_VAL` is dollars, and `acs_DEP`/`acs_REX` are ratios/index values.
{category}value.long_description: Value for the measure identified by the `measure` column, taken unchanged from the census standard file (see each level's source documentation for definition and unit). Rows with missing values are dropped, so counties where a small-population estimate could not be computed have fewer rows than the full geography x year grid. Note that `acs_VAL` (median home value) is nominal dollars and not inflation-adjusted. The `acs_PCT_*` sex shares and age-band shares each sum to exactly 1 within a geography-year, but the seven race/ethnicity shares sum to slightly less (median 0.999, as low as 0.88) because non-Hispanic 'some other race alone' has no category of its own — do not treat the race shares as a complete partition. ACS and PEP shares are not interchangeable either: the two programs use different methodologies and race/ethnicity classifications, which is why `source` distinguishes them rather than the two being reconciled.
